title: Fix sudo 'a password is required' error in scripts and cron jobs
summary: A script or cron job has no keyboard to type a password, so sudo stops with 'a password is required'. Check your sudo rights, then run the job as root from root's crontab instead of calling sudo inside it.
error_patterns: sudo: a terminal is required to read the password

aliases.text: sudo in bash script password prompt
sudo a password is required ошибка
скрипт не может выполнить sudo без пароля

prerequisites: An account in the sudo group (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint) or wheel group (Fedora, Arch, openSUSE)
A terminal window where you can type your password

steps.explain: Reproduce the problem. -n tells sudo not to ask for a password, and 'true' does nothing. If you see this message, sudo needs a typed password, and a script or cron job cannot type one.
steps.expect: sudo: a password is required (if nothing is printed, sudo works without a password here)

steps.explain: List your groups. An administrator account is in the group sudo (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint) or wheel (Fedora, Arch, openSUSE). If you are in neither group, sudo does not work for your account at all.
steps.expect: Your user name followed by the groups, for example: tester sudo

steps.explain: List what sudo allows without a password. A command that must run as root from a script needs a NOPASSWD entry here. If the output is the 'password is required' message, no rule works without a password.
steps.expect: Either 'sudo: a password is required', or a list of allowed commands; a NOPASSWD line appears only if sudo can run without a password

steps.explain: Show root's crontab, read-only. Jobs in root's crontab run as root and never ask for a password. Type your own password here, in the terminal, never inside the script.
steps.expect: The existing root jobs, or 'no crontab for root' if it is empty

steps.explain: Open root's crontab in an editor and add the job: the same schedule and command as your script's cron line, but without the word sudo in front of the command. Save and close the editor.
steps.expect: An editor opens with root's jobs; after you save, the new job is installed

steps.explain: Check your own crontab without sudo. Delete the old line that calls sudo, so the job does not run twice.
steps.expect: Your own jobs, or 'no crontab for' and your name if you have none; the old line with sudo should be removed

verify.expect: Your job line appears here, with no sudo in front of the command

rollback.explain: Undo: run sudo crontab -u root -e and delete the line you added. Then run crontab -e as your own user and put the old line back, with sudo, if you still need it.

warnings: Root's crontab runs the command with full root rights. Check the script path and what the script does before you add it.
Adding a NOPASSWD rule in sudoers lets your account run that command as root without a password. Do not do it unless your system administrator asks you to.
Never put a sudo password into a script or a cron line.
